children: plans to launch a tokenized deposit service for Japanese companies in 2026, enabling 24/7 cross-border payments, including nights and weekends, according to a report by Nikkei Asia.

The service will use Citi Token Services, the company's existing tokenization platform based on permissioned blockchain technology, to enable real-time international transactions between participating banks.

According to the Nikkei report, the company plans to become the first foreign bank to offer tokenized deposit-based international transfers to Japanese companies. The service is expected to support instant cross-border payments across five countries.
Citigroup’s global head of service, Shahmir Khaliq, told Nikkei that the service allows companies to send payments at any time without prior arrangements or risk management.

title: Citi eyes first-mover role with 24/7 tokenized payments in Japan
